note: Mat4, the units it carries and the frames it maps between. Run 2026-09-20: fifteen mutants, fourteen caught, one declared survivor, none invalid. Three are the row/column-major transpositions the file exists to prevent, and one -- the rigid inverse computing -R t instead of -R^T t -- is not hypothetical: it is the defect this task actually shipped into the working tree and the round-trip test caught, 1.9 m out at a scale of 1 m. Three more came with the frames (ADR 0021), and one of those found a hole in a test rather than in the code: retargetFrame was checked by retargeting back and comparing, which cancels any fault applied twice, so a retargetFrame that transposed its argument passed. The test compares elements directly now. Most of what the frames buy cannot be mutated at all, being a compile-time refusal; those claims are static_asserts that were each inverted and watched failing instead.

mutants.name: the perspective divide multiplies by w
mutants.find:

                p.xyz.y.value() / p.w.value(),
                p.xyz.z.value() / p.w.value(),
mutants.replace:
p.xyz.x.value() * p.w.value(),
                p.xyz.y.value() * p.w.value(),
                p.xyz.z.value() * p.w.value(),
mutants.why: Nothing in M1-09 evaluates the divide numerically: its only assertion about perspectiveDivide is the static_assert on the reference it returns, which a sign or an operator does not change. The numerical claim belongs to M1-10, and this mutant is declared surviving here rather than closed by a test invented for it (VERIFICATION.md rule 19). **Caught by M1-10 on 2026-09-21, and this entry was wrong about where.** It said M1-10's near-plane test would catch it. Measured before M1-10's tests were written: at a near plane of 1 m the depth numerator and denominator are the same number, so `n/n` and `n*n` are both 1 and the near-plane case accepts every wrong divide constructible. M1-10 therefore runs that case at five near planes, none of them 1 m, and the kill is shared by the near-plane, ten-times-near, monotonic and depth-precision cases. The lesson is this file's own: **a prediction about which test will catch a mutant is not a measurement**, and writing one down unverified is how a mutation record decays into a claim nobody checked.
